sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: This is our special Halloween episode, so I'm going to turn up a little bit of this, a little of this,
sentences.zh: 这是我们的万圣节特别节目，所以我打算调大一点这个，再调大一点那个，

sentences.en: just to get us in the mood.
sentences.zh: 好让我们进入状态。

sentences.en: Oh, and here, here's some loons.
sentences.zh: 哦，还有这个，这是潜鸟的叫声。

sentences.en: Loons are creepy.
sentences.zh: 潜鸟听起来真让人毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: A couple of weekends ago, the whole 99PI team got together to do something none of us had done since we were 13 and at slumber parties.
sentences.zh: 几个周末前，整个《99%隐形》团队聚在一起，做了一件我们从13岁参加睡衣派对以来就没做过的事。

sentences.en: I feel like we need to, like, recite something firSt.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们得先背诵点什么。

sentences.en: And it basically sounds exactly like it did when we were 13 at slumber parties.
sentences.zh: 听起来基本上和我们13岁在睡衣派对上时一模一样。

sentences.en: Who's there?
sentences.zh: 谁在那儿？

sentences.en: You're pushing it.
sentences.zh: 你有点过分了。

sentences.en: You're up.
sentences.zh: 轮到你了。

sentences.en: You are.
sentences.zh: 确实是。

sentences.en: That night at my house, we turned out all the lights and lit candles
sentences.zh: 那天晚上在我家，我们关掉了所有的灯，点上蜡烛，

sentences.en: and attempted to summon the spirit world with a Ouija board.
sentences.zh: 试图用通灵板召唤灵界。

sentences.en: That's producer Katie Mingle.
sentences.zh: 那是制片人凯蒂·明格尔。

sentences.en: She was our host that evening.
sentences.zh: 她是那天晚上的主持人。

sentences.en: You've got to rest your fingers on it.
sentences.zh: 你得把手指放在上面。

sentences.en: We were using a homemade board that Avery designed in the style of a store-bought Ouija board.
sentences.zh: 我们用的是艾弗里设计的一个自制板，仿照市面上买的通灵板样式。

sentences.en: Two arced rows of letters, the top row A through M, the second row N through Z,
sentences.zh: 两排弧形的字母，第一排从A到M，第二排从N到Z，

sentences.en: and then below the letters, a straight row of all the single-digit numbers.
sentences.zh: 在字母下方，是一排整齐的个位数数字。

sentences.en: And then, of course, yes and no in the upper left and right corners, respectively,
sentences.zh: 当然，左上角和右上角分别写着“是”和“否”，

sentences.en: and goodbye at the bottom of the board.
sentences.zh: 板子底部写着“再见”。

sentences.en: So the way Ouija is supposed to work is participants, usually two, though sometimes more,
sentences.zh: 通灵板的运作方式通常是参与者，一般是两人，有时更多，

sentences.en: ask a question to the spirits.
sentences.zh: 向灵体提问。

sentences.en: And then they, the participants, lightly rest their fingers on a planchette,
sentences.zh: 然后他们，也就是参与者，轻轻地把手指放在指示板上，

sentences.en: which is the pointer that slides around the board.
sentences.zh: 也就是那个在板子上滑动的指针。

sentences.en: And you're not supposed to push the planchette, Sam Greenspan.
sentences.zh: 山姆·格林斯潘，你不应该去推那个指示板。

sentences.en: You're supposed to allow the spirits to guide it around the board,
sentences.zh: 你应该让灵体引导它在板子上移动，

sentences.en: indicating what letters or words they're attempting to communicate.
sentences.zh: 指出他们试图传达的字母或单词。

sentences.en: E-Q-U-P?
sentences.zh: E-Q-U-P？

sentences.en: The Ouija board is so simple and iconic, and it looks like it comes from another time,
sentences.zh: 通灵板非常简单且具有标志性，看起来像是来自另一个时代，

sentences.en: like it has real history, which it turns out is more than just good design.
sentences.zh: 仿佛有着真正的历史，事实证明，这不仅仅是因为设计得好。

sentences.en: People have been gathering around a board like this one for about 130 years.
sentences.zh: 人们围着这样的板子聚会已经有大约130年了。

sentences.en: Hi, my name's Robert Merch.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我叫罗伯特·默奇。

sentences.en: Most people call me Merch.
sentences.zh: 大多数人叫我默奇。

sentences.en: And I'm considered the world's foremost expert on Ouija and talking boards.
sentences.zh: 我被认为是世界上通灵板和谈话板方面的头号专家。

sentences.en: Merch also collects boards and all sorts of other Ouija-related artifacts.
sentences.zh: 默奇还收藏各种板子以及其他与通灵板相关的文物。

sentences.en: So this stuff is everywhere.
sentences.zh: 所以这些东西到处都是。

sentences.en: You know, I frame things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我喜欢装裱东西。

sentences.en: The arrangement I have with my husband is that I can only put things on the wall that can be framed.
sentences.zh: 我和我丈夫的约定是，我只能把能装裱的东西挂在墙上。

sentences.en: Now, when he made that agreement, he didn't realize that I could frame anything.
sentences.zh: 当时他达成这个协议时，没意识到我什么都能装裱。

sentences.en: So, yeah, that was unfortunate for him.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，对他来说那很不幸。

sentences.en: Merch says to understand where talking boards came from, that's the generic term, talking boards,
sentences.zh: 默奇说，要了解谈话板——这是通用术语——的起源，

sentences.en: you have to go back to the middle of the 1800s, to three sisters in New York.
sentences.zh: 你得回到19世纪中叶，去纽约找三姐妹。

sentences.en: The Fox sisters, they are really what starts this explosion of mediumship and spiritualism in America and beyond.
sentences.zh: 福克斯姐妹，她们真正开启了美国乃至全球通灵和唯灵论的热潮。

sentences.en: The Fox sisters claimed to be mediums to the spirit world.
sentences.zh: 福克斯姐妹声称自己是通灵者，能与灵界沟通。

sentences.en: And in public demonstrations, they would ask questions of the spirits and receive audible knocks back on the wall.
sentences.zh: 在公开演示中，她们会向灵体提问，并收到墙上传回的敲击声作为回应。

sentences.en: Knocks that they translated into letters of the alphabet.
sentences.zh: 她们将这些敲击声翻译成字母表中的字母。

sentences.en: The Fox sisters were a sensation.
sentences.zh: 福克斯姐妹当时轰动一时。

sentences.en: They were the most visible faces of a growing movement known as spiritualism,
sentences.zh: 她们是唯灵论这一新兴运动中最引人注目的面孔，

sentences.en: which held that spirits of the dead could be contacted by the living and that they had secret knowledge to impart.
sentences.zh: 该运动认为生者可以与死者的灵魂取得联系，并且死者有秘密知识可以传授。

sentences.en: When tales of the Fox sisters swept through American newspapers, more and more people started to believe.
sentences.zh: 当福克斯姐妹的故事席卷美国报纸时，越来越多的人开始相信。

sentences.en: During and after the Civil War, spiritualism became even more important to people.
sentences.zh: 在内战期间及之后，唯灵论对人们变得更加重要。

sentences.en: Everyone had, you know, whether it was a father, a son, a grandfather, an uncle, you know, they all lost somebody.
sentences.zh: 每个人，你知道，无论是父亲、儿子、祖父还是叔叔，他们都失去了亲人。

sentences.en: People just went away and they didn't come back.
sentences.zh: 人们就这样离开了，再也没有回来。

sentences.en: So, what else are you going to do?
sentences.zh: 所以，你还能做什么呢？

sentences.en: You know, you turn to trying to make contact with these people who are gone.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你只能转而尝试与这些逝去的人取得联系。

sentences.en: And in 1886, the fledgling Associated Press ran an article in papers all over the country
sentences.zh: 1886年，刚起步的美联社在全国各地的报纸上刊登了一篇文章，

sentences.en: about these new talking boards coming out of the spiritualist movement in Ohio.
sentences.zh: 讲述了这些源自俄亥俄州唯灵论运动的新型谈话板。

sentences.en: It's unclear whether he read the article, but a few years later, in 1890,
sentences.zh: 不清楚他是否读过那篇文章，但几年后的1890年，

sentences.en: a businessman named Charles Kennard of Baltimore, Maryland,
sentences.zh: 一位名叫查尔斯·肯纳德的马里兰州巴尔的摩商人，

sentences.en: realized this talking board could make him lots and lots of money.
sentences.zh: 意识到这种谈话板能让他赚到大钱。

sentences.en: Kennard pulled together a small group of investors
sentences.zh: 肯纳德召集了一小群投资者，

sentences.en: and formed the Kennard Novelty Company to exclusively make and market talking boards.
sentences.zh: 成立了肯纳德新奇公司，专门制造和销售谈话板。

sentences.en: Contrary to popular belief, the name Ouija is not a combination of the French and German words for yes, we, and yeah.
sentences.zh: 与普遍看法相反，Ouija这个名字并不是法语和德语中“是”的组合。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Merch says that according to documents belonging to the original founders of the company,
sentences.zh: 默奇说，根据公司创始人的文件记载，

sentences.en: they sat down and asked the board itself what it wanted to be called.
sentences.zh: 他们坐下来问板子自己想叫什么名字。

sentences.en: And letter by letter, it spells out O-U-I-J-A.
sentences.zh: 然后它逐个字母拼出了O-U-I-J-A。

sentences.en: And when they ask the board what that means, the board spells out good luck.
sentences.zh: 当他们问板子那是什么意思时，板子拼出了“好运”。

sentences.en: They called the board Ouija, the Egyptian luck board.
sentences.zh: 他们把这块板子称为Ouija，即埃及幸运板。

sentences.en: They added Egyptian just for a little exotic flair.
sentences.zh: 他们加上“埃及”只是为了增加一点异国情调。

sentences.en: The patented Ouija board looked a lot like the talking boards that came out of the spiritualist movement.
sentences.zh: 获得专利的通灵板看起来和唯灵论运动中出现的谈话板很像。

sentences.en: The only real substantial change was that the Ouija board put the letters of the alphabet in a double arc
sentences.zh: 唯一实质性的改变是，通灵板将字母表排成了双弧线，

sentences.en: instead of two straight lines across.
sentences.zh: 而不是横跨的两条直线。

sentences.en: There have been a few small design changes since the early boards.
sentences.zh: 自早期的板子以来，设计上有一些小的改动。

sentences.en: For example, there was once a full moon and a crescent moon in the top left and right-hand corners.
sentences.zh: 例如，曾经在左上角和右上角有一个满月和一个新月。

sentences.en: Eventually, the full moon became a sun, which is what you see now.
sentences.zh: 最终，满月变成了太阳，也就是你现在看到的。

sentences.en: But through the years, the brand has always been very identifiable.
sentences.zh: 但多年来，这个品牌一直非常有辨识度。

sentences.en: So the Ouija board has always been very simple.
sentences.zh: 所以通灵板一直都很简单。

sentences.en: Anyone who looked at it would know, okay, that's a Ouija board.
sentences.zh: 任何看到它的人都会知道，哦，那是通灵板。

sentences.en: By 1893, Charles Kennard had left the company, and it was taken over by William Fold,
sentences.zh: 到1893年，查尔斯·肯纳德离开了公司，公司由威廉·福尔德接管，

sentences.en: who had come to be known as the father of Ouija.
sentences.zh: 他后来被称为“通灵板之父”。

sentences.en: Fold's New York Times obituary actually credited him with inventing the board,
sentences.zh: 福尔德在《纽约时报》的讣告中甚至称他发明了这块板子，

sentences.en: which, of course, he did not do.
sentences.zh: 当然，他并没有发明它。

sentences.en: But he was incredibly good at selling it.
sentences.zh: 但他非常擅长推销它。

sentences.en: Instead of being a straight-up evangelist for the boards, he'd purport to be one of the skeptics.
sentences.zh: 他没有直接成为板子的传道者，而是假装自己是怀疑论者之一。

sentences.en: He would say, I don't believe in the Ouija board.
sentences.zh: 他会说，我不相信通灵板。

sentences.en: You know, I'm no spiritualiSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不是唯灵论者。

sentences.en: I'm a Presbyterian.
sentences.zh: 我是长老会教徒。

sentences.en: And then at the same time, same interview, he would say,
sentences.zh: 但同时，在同一次采访中，他会说，

sentences.en: but we lost the shipment of Ouija boards on the train tracks,
sentences.zh: 但是我们有一批通灵板在铁轨上丢失了，

sentences.en: and we asked the board where they were, and it told us.
sentences.zh: 我们问板子它们在哪里，它告诉了我们。

sentences.en: And then they went down that track, and sure enough,
sentences.zh: 然后他们沿着那条轨道走去，果然，

sentences.en: they found that the train had derailed, and we found all our boards.
sentences.zh: 他们发现火车脱轨了，我们也找到了所有的板子。

sentences.en: Whether the board worked and how it worked,
sentences.zh: 板子是否有效以及它是如何运作的，

sentences.en: whether it was just a game or a more serious spiritual tool,
sentences.zh: 它究竟只是一个游戏还是一个更严肃的通灵工具，

sentences.en: was something Fold kept intentionally mysterious.
sentences.zh: 福尔德一直让它保持神秘感。

sentences.en: And this marketing strategy was extremely successful.
sentences.zh: 这种营销策略非常成功。

sentences.en: Hey, everyone had one.
sentences.zh: 嘿，每个人都有一个。

sentences.en: People played at home with their families.
sentences.zh: 人们在家里和家人一起玩。

sentences.en: Ladies played at tea parties.
sentences.zh: 女士们在茶会上玩。

sentences.en: In fact, one of the boards in Merch's collection doubles as a tea tray.
sentences.zh: 事实上，默奇收藏的一块板子还可以兼作茶盘。

sentences.en: People even played with their little kids, which might seem kind of weird now.
sentences.zh: 人们甚至和他们的小孩子一起玩，这在现在看来可能有点奇怪。

sentences.en: Fast forward a couple of decades, around 1920,
sentences.zh: 快进几十年，大约在1920年左右，

sentences.en: and Ouija is still good, clean, family fun.
sentences.zh: 通灵板仍然是一种健康、纯粹的家庭娱乐。

sentences.en: And, it turned out, it was also a great thing to do on a date.
sentences.zh: 而且，事实证明，它也是约会时的一项绝佳活动。

sentences.en: So you're coming out of Victorian times when men and women are not supposed to be alone together.
sentences.zh: 那时候你正走出维多利亚时代，当时男女不应该单独相处。

sentences.en: They're not supposed to be in the dark together.
sentences.zh: 他们不应该在黑暗中待在一起。

sentences.en: They're not supposed to be touching.
sentences.zh: 他们不应该有身体接触。

sentences.en: So the original Ouija board would be placed on your lap.
sentences.zh: 所以最初的通灵板会放在你的膝盖上。

sentences.en: Your knees would be touching.
sentences.zh: 你们的膝盖会碰到一起。

sentences.en: Your fingers would be touching on the planchette.
sentences.zh: 你们的手指会在指示板上接触。

sentences.en: You know, you would be doing it by candlelight.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你们会在烛光下进行。

sentences.en: And you can see really quickly that the directions add in, you know,
sentences.zh: 你可以很快看出说明书里加了，你知道，

sentences.en: two people, a man and a woman prefer.
sentences.zh: 两个人，一男一女更佳。

sentences.en: And if you need proof of what a normal part of Americana the Ouija board was,
sentences.zh: 如果你需要证据证明通灵板是美国文化中多么正常的一部分，

sentences.en: look no further than the king of Americana himself, Norman Rockwell.
sentences.zh: 看看美国文化之王诺曼·洛克威尔就知道了。

sentences.en: In 1920, he made a painting of a man and a woman in the position Murch just described.
sentences.zh: 1920年，他画了一幅画，画中男女处于默奇刚才描述的位置。

sentences.en: Knees touching, he looking flirtatiously at her, a Ouija board resting in their laps.
sentences.zh: 膝盖相触，他调情地看着她，一块通灵板放在他们的膝盖上。

sentences.en: Of course, Ouija always had a few naysayers.
sentences.zh: 当然，通灵板总是有一些反对者。

sentences.en: And some of the first and loudest were actually the people whose jobs these talking boards had just stolen.
sentences.zh: 其中最早且声音最大的，实际上就是那些饭碗被这些谈话板抢走的人。

sentences.en: We see mediums actually saying,
sentences.zh: 我们看到通灵者实际上在说，

sentences.en: these things are dangerous.
sentences.zh: 这些东西很危险。

sentences.en: You don't know what kind of doors you're opening.
sentences.zh: 你不知道你打开的是什么样的大门。

sentences.en: You need someone like me who's experienced to guide you through this unseen world.
sentences.zh: 你需要像我这样有经验的人来引导你穿过这个看不见的世界。

sentences.en: Now, why would they say that?
sentences.zh: 那么，他们为什么要这么说呢？

sentences.en: Well, because it's cutting into their profession, their money.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为这影响了他们的职业，他们的收入。

sentences.en: But naysayers stayed on the fringe through the years.
sentences.zh: 但多年来，反对者一直处于边缘地位。

sentences.en: Oh, sure, there'd be the occasional the Ouija board told me to do it murder that would make it into the news.
sentences.zh: 哦，当然，偶尔会有“通灵板告诉我这么做”的谋杀案登上新闻。

sentences.en: But they were few and far between.
sentences.zh: 但这类事件非常罕见。

sentences.en: Throughout the decades, Ouija mostly held on to its wholesome reputation.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，通灵板大多保持着它健康的名声。

sentences.en: Until.
sentences.zh: 直到。

sentences.en: Ugh, The ExorciSt.
sentences.zh: 呃，《驱魔人》。

sentences.en: Released in 1973, I had to sleep in my parents' bedroom for a week after I saw this when I was a kid.
sentences.zh: 1973年上映，我小时候看完后，不得不跟我父母睡了一个星期的卧室。

sentences.en: The way!
sentences.zh: 走开！

sentences.en: The soul is mine!
sentences.zh: 灵魂是我的！

sentences.en: At the beginning of the movie, the main character's mother discovers she's been playing with a Ouija board.
sentences.zh: 电影开头，主角的母亲发现她一直在玩通灵板。

sentences.en: The Exorcist is really the first big media moment that infers that playing a Ouija board by yourself could lead to demonic possession.
sentences.zh: 《驱魔人》确实是第一个暗示独自玩通灵板可能导致恶魔附身的重大媒体时刻。

sentences.en: The following years saw the Ouija board denounced by religious groups as Satan's preferred method of communication.
sentences.zh: 随后的几年里，通灵板被宗教团体谴责为撒旦首选的交流方式。

sentences.en: Ouija boards aren't harmless.
sentences.zh: 通灵板并不无害。

sentences.en: Seances aren't harmless.
sentences.zh: 降神会并不无害。

sentences.en: Listen, don't be playing games on Halloween.
sentences.zh: 听着，万圣节别玩这些游戏。

sentences.en: Don't call on demons because they'll come and live with you.
sentences.zh: 别召唤恶魔，因为它们会来和你住在一起。

sentences.en: The Bible says, he who seeks evil, evil will come to him.
sentences.zh: 圣经说，寻求邪恶的人，邪恶必临到他。

sentences.en: Pat Robertson is pretty extreme.
sentences.zh: 帕特·罗伯逊有点极端。

sentences.en: But still, the image of the board changed a lot since that Norman Rockwell painting in 1920.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，自1920年那幅诺曼·洛克威尔的画以来，人们对这块板子的印象已经发生了很大变化。

sentences.en: Parker Brothers, and later Hasbro, which acquired Parker Brothers in 1991, still sells a lot of boards.
sentences.zh: 派克兄弟，以及后来在1991年收购了派克兄弟的孩之宝，仍然销售大量的板子。

sentences.en: But the reason people buy them has changed.
sentences.zh: 但人们购买它们的原因已经改变了。

sentences.en: It's not good, clean family fun anymore.
sentences.zh: 它不再是那种健康、纯粹的家庭娱乐了。

sentences.en: Now people buy them because they want to get scared.
sentences.zh: 现在人们买它是因为想寻求刺激。

sentences.en: There's another Ouija movie just released called Ouija, which will do nothing to change the board's sinister reputation.
sentences.zh: 最近又上映了一部叫《死亡占卜》的电影，这只会加深人们对这种占卜板阴森恐怖的印象。

sentences.en: Come on, you guys.
sentences.zh: 得了吧，你们几个。

sentences.en: Who's doing that?
sentences.zh: 谁在搞鬼？

sentences.en: Sarah, cut it out!
sentences.zh: 莎拉，别闹了！

sentences.en: I'm not pushing it.
sentences.zh: 我没推它。

sentences.en: Just spelled high friend.
sentences.zh: 刚才拼出来的是“好朋友”。

sentences.en: Okay, this is freaking me out.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这真的把我吓到了。

sentences.en: I'm done with this.
sentences.zh: 我不玩了。

sentences.en: But a sinister reputation is fine with Hasbro.
sentences.zh: 但孩之宝公司并不介意这种阴森的声誉。

sentences.en: In fact, they put up a lot of the money for that new Ouija movie.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们为那部新的《死亡占卜》电影投入了大量资金。

sentences.en: They've also released a new version of the game and changed the tagline, which used to be...
sentences.zh: 他们还发布了游戏的新版本，并更改了宣传语，以前的宣传语是……

sentences.en: It's just a game, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这只是个游戏，不是吗？

sentences.en: The new tagline?
sentences.zh: 新的宣传语呢？

sentences.en: Do not play the Ouija board if you think it's just a game.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得这只是个游戏，那就别玩占卜板。

sentences.en: The design of the new board is different, too.
sentences.zh: 新版占卜板的设计也不同了。

sentences.en: For the first time in a very long time,
sentences.zh: 在经历了很长一段时间后，

sentences.en: the Ouija board got a makeover.
sentences.zh: 占卜板终于改头换面了。

sentences.en: They've added a couple of modern features, like a purple light in the planchette.
sentences.zh: 他们增加了一些现代功能，比如指示器里的紫光灯。

sentences.en: But overall, they've tried to make the board look older than the classic board.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，他们试图让这块板子看起来比经典款更古老。

sentences.en: It's brown and kind of weathered, and it looks like something you might find on a pirate ship.
sentences.zh: 它呈棕色，看起来有些风化，就像你在海盗船上可能会发现的东西一样。

sentences.en: They've really gone for the older look, which is neat, because again, people assume these boards have been around for thousands of years, which we know isn't true.
sentences.zh: 他们确实追求了那种复古感，这很有意思，因为人们总是认为这些板子已经存在几千年了，而我们知道事实并非如此。

sentences.en: But belief is important to the Ouija board.
sentences.zh: 但“相信”对占卜板来说很重要。

sentences.en: Belief is very important to the Ouija board, especially subconscious beliefs.
sentences.zh: “相信”对占卜板非常重要，尤其是潜意识里的信念。

sentences.en: Which brings us, finally, to how these things work.
sentences.zh: 这最终让我们回到了这些东西是如何运作的问题上。

sentences.en: Basically, when it comes to the Ouija board, the reason that it seems to work, it feels as if it works, is down to something called the idiomotor effect.
sentences.zh: 基本上，谈到占卜板，它之所以看起来能用，感觉上能用，归根结底是因为一种叫做“意动效应”的东西。

sentences.en: And what that is, essentially, is non-conscious muscular movements.
sentences.zh: 本质上，这就是指无意识的肌肉运动。

sentences.en: That's Professor Chris French.
sentences.zh: 那是克里斯·弗伦奇教授。

sentences.en: I am head of the Anomalistic Psychology Research Unit at Goldsmiths University of London.
sentences.zh: 我是伦敦大学金史密斯学院异常心理学研究部门的负责人。

sentences.en: And before you ask, anomalistic psychology is the psychology of weird stuff.
sentences.zh: 在你问之前先说明一下，异常心理学就是研究那些怪异现象的心理学。

sentences.en: The term idiomotor effect was first coined by an English physician and researcher named William Benjamin Carpenter back in 1852,
sentences.zh: “意动效应”这个术语最早是由英国医生兼研究员威廉·本杰明·卡彭特在1852年提出的，

sentences.en: right when spiritualism was starting to become popular both in Europe and the U.S.
sentences.zh: 当时唯灵论正开始在欧洲和美国流行起来。

sentences.en: So the idiomotor effect applies in the case of Ouija, in that our bodies are making small subconscious movements
sentences.zh: 所以意动效应适用于占卜板的情况，即我们的身体在暗示或某种潜意识知识的引导下，

sentences.en: that are guided by a suggestion or some subconscious knowledge.
sentences.zh: 做出了细微的潜意识运动。

sentences.en: And so particularly, once the first letter or two has been made apparent, then you kind of get an idea of what's going to come next.
sentences.zh: 特别是当第一个或前两个字母显现出来后，你就会对接下来会出现什么有个大概的预感。

sentences.en: So if it was spelling out a name and it's spelt out the letter B and then an O, you might well be thinking, no, it's probably going to be Bob.
sentences.zh: 所以如果它正在拼写一个名字，已经拼出了B和O，你很可能就会想，不，后面大概会是Bob。

sentences.en: And the idiomotor effect becomes magnified as more people play.
sentences.zh: 而且随着参与人数的增加，意动效应会被放大。

sentences.en: One of the very interesting things that happens when you talk to people who have played around with Ouija boards
sentences.zh: 当你和玩过占卜板的人交谈时，一件非常有趣的事情是，

sentences.en: is that they will very often claim that they've got answers from the Ouija board that nobody around the board actually knew that.
sentences.zh: 他们经常声称从占卜板上得到了在场所有人都不知道的答案。

sentences.en: So that proves that it was some kind of external agency.
sentences.zh: 所以这证明了它是某种外部力量在起作用。

sentences.en: Professor French says that what's happening here is that our subconscious mind does actually know the answer.
sentences.zh: 弗伦奇教授说，这里发生的情况是，我们的潜意识确实知道答案。

sentences.en: Our conscious mind just can't access the information.
sentences.zh: 只是我们的意识无法获取这些信息。

sentences.en: And researchers are so convinced of this, they've even used Ouija boards to study our subconscious.
sentences.zh: 研究人员对此深信不疑，他们甚至利用占卜板来研究我们的潜意识。

sentences.en: So for example, in one of these studies, participants were asked simple fact-based questions like,
sentences.zh: 例如，在其中一项研究中，参与者被问及一些简单的事实性问题，比如，

sentences.en: it's Buenos Aires, the capital of Brazil.
sentences.zh: 布宜诺斯艾利斯是巴西的首都。

sentences.en: They got the answers right about 50% of the time.
sentences.zh: 他们大约有50%的题目答对了。

sentences.en: But when they used a Ouija board to help them answer the same questions...
sentences.zh: 但当他们使用占卜板来辅助回答同样的问题时……

sentences.en: They actually got higher scores then.
sentences.zh: 他们的得分确实更高了。

sentences.en: They got the answers right about 65% of the time.
sentences.zh: 他们大约有65%的题目答对了。

sentences.en: So in other words, they did know the answer, even if they couldn't consciously access it.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们确实知道答案，即使他们无法有意识地提取出来。

sentences.en: There have been all kinds of studies done on paranormal experiences.
sentences.zh: 人们已经对超自然体验进行了各种各样的研究。

sentences.en: And Professor French says they never reveal an external or spiritual force at work.
sentences.zh: 弗伦奇教授说，这些研究从未揭示出有外部或精神力量在起作用。

sentences.en: They always reveal an internal force at work, even if it's a subconscious one.
sentences.zh: 它们总是揭示出内部力量在起作用，即使是潜意识的力量。

sentences.en: I don't have any doubts in my mind that we can explain the vast majority of ostensibly paranormal experiences
sentences.zh: 我毫不怀疑，我们可以通过心理学来解释绝大多数表面上的超自然体验。

sentences.en: by looking to psychology.
sentences.zh: 至于我们是否能解释每一个案例，那就是价值六万四千美元的问题了。

sentences.en: Whether or not we can explain every single one is the $64,000 question.
sentences.zh: 刚才不是有个R吗？

sentences.en: Wasn't there an R?
sentences.zh: 是啊，F-I。

sentences.en: Yeah, F-I.
sentences.zh: 刚才有R吗？

sentences.en: Was there an R?
sentences.zh: 当我们在我家玩占卜板时，指示器的移动似乎不太像是受意动效应支配，

sentences.en: When we played Ouija at my house, the planchette seemed less to be governed by the ideomotor effect
sentences.zh: 而更多是受惯性定律支配。

sentences.en: and more by the law of inertia.
sentences.zh: 我不知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: I don't know what's going on.
sentences.zh: 什么都没发生。

sentences.en: Nothing.
sentences.zh: 基本上，它根本没动。

sentences.en: Essentially, it's not moving.
sentences.zh: 我们的体验并不怎么奇怪或令人毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: And our experience wasn't terribly strange or creepy.
sentences.zh: 大部分时间只是很慢。

sentences.en: It was mostly just slow.
sentences.zh: 它好像在动。

sentences.en: It's kind of moving.
sentences.zh: 看，它动了一点点。

sentences.en: Look, it moved a little bit.
sentences.zh: 但默奇玩过很多次，确实有过一些奇怪的经历。

sentences.en: But Murch has played enough times to have had some weird experiences.
sentences.zh: 有些时候，我认为只是人在推它，而他们自己没意识到。

sentences.en: Some, I think, are just the person pushing it and they don't know it.
sentences.zh: 这显然是意动反应。

sentences.en: It's clearly ideomotor response.
sentences.zh: 还有些时候，它回答的问题太离奇了，让人纳闷它怎么会知道？

sentences.en: Other times, it's answered things that just seem so bizarre that how would it know?
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你能和灵界交流，为什么占卜板不能用呢？

sentences.en: You know, if you can talk to the spirit world, why wouldn't the Ouija board work?
sentences.zh: 真正的问题是，你能和灵界取得联系吗？

sentences.en: And the real question is, can you make contact with the spirit world?
sentences.zh: 这个问题从古至今一直困扰着人类。

sentences.en: And that's a question that has been dogging humanity since the beginning of time.
sentences.zh: 从有人第一次意识到人死后无法复生开始，就是如此。

sentences.en: Since the first time someone realized when they died, they didn't come back.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上大家都离开我家后，我独自坐在沙发上。

sentences.en: After everyone left my house that night, I was sitting on my couch by myself.
sentences.zh: 周围非常安静。

sentences.en: It was really quiet.
sentences.zh: 我还没吹灭所有的蜡烛，所以气氛有点特别。

sentences.en: I hadn't blown out all the candles yet, so there was kind of a mood.
sentences.zh: 然后，我其中一个弹簧窗帘猛地弹了上去，把我吓得魂飞魄散。

sentences.en: And then, one of my spring-loaded blinds slammed up and scared the s*** out of me.
sentences.zh: 我不得不承认，我看着那个占卜板，有一瞬间我心想，这只是个游戏，不是吗？

sentences.en: And I have to admit, I looked at the Ouija board and I wondered, just for a second, it's just a game, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 占卜板啊，你会为我工作吗？

sentences.en: The Ouija boards, would you work for me?
sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook上找到并关注这个节目。

sentences.zh: 我们所有人都开通了Twitter、Instagram和Spotify账号。

sentences.zh: 并收听《99% Invisible》的所有剧集，你必须访问99pi.org。
